meaning: So that is why / it follows that.

examples.reading: どうりでねむいわけだ。

examples.japanese: 三年も住んでいるから、日本語が上手なわけだ。
examples.reading: さんねんもすんでいるから、にほんごがじょうずなわけだ。
examples.gloss: He has lived here for three years, so of course his Japanese is good.

examples.japanese: 今日は祭りだから、人が多いわけだ。
examples.reading: きょうはまつりだから、ひとがおおいわけだ。
examples.gloss: Today is a festival, so no wonder there are so many people.

usage: Draws a conclusion that follows from what you already know.
わけがない means "there is no way". わけではない softens a statement: it is not that…
Nouns and な-adjectives link with の and な.

compare.difference: はずだ is an expectation about the future or the unknown. わけだ explains a known fact.
